points.title: 童年与教育
points.description: 艾米莉·狄金森出生于马萨诸塞州阿默斯特的一个显赫家庭，父亲是爱德华·狄金森，一位成功的律师和国会议员。她在家中接受了良好的教育，包括古典文学、宗教和科学。这一时期，她展现出对诗歌和文学的浓厚兴趣，开始创作自己的诗歌。阿默斯特的乡村生活和严格的清教徒传统对她后来的创作产生了深远影响，塑造了她独特的世界观和诗歌风格。
points.descriptionEn: Emily Dickinson was born into a prominent family in Amherst, Massachusetts, where her father Edward Dickinson was a successful lawyer and U.S. Congressman. She received an excellent education at home, including classical literature, religion, and science. During this period, she developed a strong interest in poetry and literature, beginning to compose her own works. The rural life of Amherst and the strict Puritan traditions profoundly influenced her later creative work, shaping her unique worldview and poetic style.

points.title: 蒙特霍利约克学院
points.description: 1847年，狄金森进入南哈利附近的蒙特霍利约克女子学院学习。这是她唯一接受的正规高等教育经历。在校期间，她表现出色，但仅学习了一年就因健康原因和宗教质疑而退学。这段短暂的高等教育经历虽然短暂，却为她提供了接触更广阔思想世界的窗口，同时也加深了她对宗教教义的质疑，这种质疑后来成为她诗歌中反复探讨的主题之一。
points.descriptionEn: In 1847, Dickinson attended Mount Holyoke Female Seminary in South Hadley, the only formal higher education she ever received. During her time there, she excelled academically but left after only one year due to health concerns and religious doubts. Although this brief period of higher education was short-lived, it provided her with a window to a broader intellectual world and deepened her questioning of religious doctrines, a theme that would become recurrent in her poetry.

points.title: 隐居创作期
points.description: 回到阿默斯特后，狄金森逐渐开始她的隐居生活。这一时期，她创作了大量诗歌，但很少发表。她与家人住在父亲的大房子里，过着相对封闭的生活。1855年，她结识了牧师查尔斯·沃兹沃斯，成为她生命中重要的精神交流对象。1858-1862年间，她进入创作高峰期，创作了近800首诗歌，并开始将诗歌装订成册。这一阶段的作品展现了她对死亡、爱情、自然和信仰等主题的深刻思考，形成了她独特的诗歌风格。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Amherst, Dickinson gradually began her reclusive life. During this period, she wrote a large number of poems but rarely published them. She lived with her family in her father's large house, leading a relatively secluded existence. In 1855, she met the Reverend Charles Wadsworth, who became an important spiritual confidant. Between 1858 and 1862, she entered a peak creative period, writing nearly 800 poems and beginning to bind them into booklets. The works from this period showcase her deep reflections on themes such as death, love, nature, and faith, forming her unique poetic style.

points.title: 成熟创作期
points.description: 1860年代是狄金森创作的成熟期。她与托马斯·温特沃斯·希金森建立了通信关系，尽管她很少采纳他的出版建议。这一时期，她的诗歌风格更加成熟，大胆使用破折号、不规则标点和独特的韵律。她继续过着隐居生活，但通过书信与外界保持联系。1864-1865年，由于健康恶化，她不得不减少写作，但她的创作质量并未下降。这一时期的作品更加深刻地探讨了生命的意义和死亡的必然性，展现了她对生命本质的独特思考。
points.descriptionEn: The 1860s marked Dickinson's mature creative period. She corresponded with Thomas Wentworth Higginson, though she rarely took his publishing advice. During this time, her poetic style became more mature, boldly using dashes, irregular punctuation, and unique rhythms. She continued her reclusive lifestyle but maintained contact with the outside world through letters. Due to declining health between 1864-1865, she had to reduce her writing output, but the quality of her work remained high. The works from this period more deeply explored the meaning of life and the inevitability of death, showcasing her unique contemplation on the essence of existence.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 狄金森的晚年健康状况持续恶化，但她仍坚持创作。1886年5月15日，她因肾脏疾病去世，享年55岁。在她生前，只有不到十首诗歌被匿名发表，且大多被大幅修改。直到她去世后，妹妹拉维妮娅才发现并整理了她的大量手稿，这些作品才逐渐被世人所知。狄金森的诗歌以其独特的风格和深刻的哲学思考而闻名，她被视为美国文学史上最重要的诗人之一，对现代诗歌产生了深远影响。她的隐居生活和神秘形象也成为文学和文化研究的重要课题。
points.descriptionEn: Dickinson's health continued to decline in her later years, but she persisted in writing. On May 15, 1886, she died of kidney disease at the age of 55. During her lifetime, fewer than ten of her poems were published anonymously, most significantly altered. Only after her death did her sister Lavinia discover and organize her extensive manuscripts, gradually bringing her work to public attention. Dickinson's poetry is renowned for its unique style and profound philosophical contemplation, establishing her as one of the most important poets in American literary history with a profound influence on modern poetry. Her reclusive lifestyle and mysterious persona have also become significant subjects of literary and cultural study.

appraisal.zh: 狄金森被公认为美国文学史上最具创新精神的诗人之一，她以简洁深刻的语言、独特韵律和大胆主题打破传统诗歌形式，开现代诗歌先河，也为女性文学传统树立榜样。也有研究者指出，其破折号与标点的非常规使用似欠技巧，主题多囿于个人体验与死亡，生前拒绝出版亦被指自我中心。但总体而言，她作为女性先驱的地位已获重新评估，作品被视为对传统性别角色的挑战。
appraisal.en: Dickinson is widely regarded as one of the most innovative poets in American literary history, breaking free from conventional poetic forms with concise, profound language, distinctive rhythms, and bold themes, pioneering modern poetry and setting an example for the female literary tradition. Some researchers note that her unconventional dashes and punctuation suggest a lack of technique, that her themes remain confined to personal experience and death, and that her refusal to publish seemed self-centered. Overall, however, her standing as a female pioneer has been reassessed, her work seen as challenging traditional gender roles.

supporter.zh: 狄金森被视为美国文学史上最具创新精神的诗人之一。她的诗歌以其简洁而深刻的语言、独特的韵律和大胆的主题探索而著称。支持者认为她打破了传统诗歌的形式束缚，开创了现代诗歌的先河。她的作品对女性文学传统做出了重要贡献，为后来的女性作家树立了榜样。尽管生前默默无闻，但她的诗歌遗产至今仍在影响着世界各地的读者和诗人，展现了真正的艺术超越时代的力量。
supporter.en: Dickinson is regarded as one of the most innovative poets in American literary history. Her poetry is celebrated for its concise yet profound language, unique rhythms, and bold thematic explorations. Supporters argue that she broke free from conventional poetic forms, pioneering modern poetry. Her work made significant contributions to the female literary tradition, setting an example for subsequent women writers. Despite her obscurity during her lifetime, her poetic legacy continues to influence readers and poets worldwide, demonstrating the true power of art to transcend time.

critic.zh: 批评者指出狄金森的诗歌存在形式上的不规则性，如过度使用破折号和不规则的标点，这可能被视为缺乏技巧或自我放纵。一些评论家认为她的主题过于局限于个人体验和死亡，缺乏更广阔的社会视野。此外，她生前拒绝出版作品的态度也被批评为一种自我中心的表现，未能充分利用她的才华服务更广泛的社会。还有人质疑她隐居生活方式的真实性，认为这可能是一种精心构建的文学形象，而非真实的生活选择。
critic.en: Critics point out that Dickinson's poetry contains formal irregularities, such as excessive use of dashes and unconventional punctuation, which may be seen as lacking technical skill or representing self-indulgence. Some commentators argue that her themes are too confined to personal experiences and death, lacking a broader social perspective. Additionally, her refusal to publish during her lifetime has been criticized as self-centered, failing to utilize her talents for the benefit of a wider society. Others question the authenticity of her reclusive lifestyle, suggesting it might be a carefully constructed literary persona rather than a genuine life choice.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，狄金森被定义为一位复杂的文学人物，她的作品超越了时代限制。学术界将她视为美国超验主义运动的重要参与者，尽管她从未公开参与这一运动。她的诗歌被重新发现后，深刻影响了20世纪的现代主义诗歌。在流行文化中，她常被描绘为神秘的隐士形象，这种形象既反映了历史事实，也融入了后世的浪漫想象。近年来，随着女性主义文学批评的发展，狄金森作为女性先驱者的地位得到了重新评估，她的作品被视为对传统性别角色的挑战和对女性声音的肯定。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Dickinson is defined as a complex literary figure whose work transcends temporal limitations. Academia regards her as an important participant in the American Transcendentalist movement, despite never publicly engaging with it. Her poetry, rediscovered after her death, profoundly influenced 20th-century modernist poetry. In popular culture, she is often portrayed as a mysterious recluse, an image that reflects historical facts while incorporating later romantic imagination. In recent years, with the development of feminist literary criticism, Dickinson's status as a female pioneer has been reassessed, with her work seen as challenging traditional gender roles and affirming female voices.

self.zh: 希望是有羽毛的东西，它栖息在灵魂中，唱着没有歌词的歌，永远不停歇。
self.en: 'Hope' is the thing with feathers - That perches in the soul - And sings the tune without the words - And never stops - at all -
